name: Javan Trogon
rangeDescription: Montane forest of western java
description: Beautiful and highly range-restricted trogon found only in Java’s far western belt of volcanoes, where it inhabits montane and foothill forests at 900-2500 meters. Unmistakable, decked out in all the colors of the rainbow: note bright red bill, yellow breast, orange belly, olive-green head and chest, glossy blue-green back, and purple-and-green bare facial skin.

name: Cinnamon Screech-Owl
rangeDescription: Cloud forest of southern ecuador to northern peru
description: Small screech-owl with a scattered distribution in the Andes. It inhabits cloud forest in southeastern Ecuador and northern Peru, as well as a few locations in Colombia and Venezuela.

name: Slender-billed Parakeet
rangeDescription: Lowlands of chile (aconcagua to northern aysén and chiloé island)
description: Fairly common, but nomadic in the Lake District region of Chile. Found in farmland with forest patches, hedges, and scattered tall trees; less of a forest bird than the smaller and duller Austral Parakeet, although the two species rarely if ever mix together.

name: Mouse-colored Penduline-Tit
rangeDescription: Thornscrub of ethiopia and somalia to far northern tanzania
description: A tiny drab bird with a sharp bill. Note gray back, whitish underparts, and faintly black-speckled forehead.

name: Orange-throated Sunangel
rangeDescription: Andes of northeastern colombia to northwestern venezuela (southern lara to táchira)
description: Medium-sized hummingbird with a short, straight bill found in the Andes of Venezuela and eastern Colombia. Male has a green body, buff and green spotted underparts, and a glittering orange throat.

name: Spot-winged Thrush
rangeDescription: Montane forest of sri lanka
description: Brown thrush with bold dark spots on the underparts, white spots in the wings, and black facial stripes below the eye. Occurs in pairs or singly, on or near the ground, in forest, forest edge, and gardens, mostly in the Wet Zone, but also locally in the Dry Zone.

name: Rufous-necked Wood-Rail
rangeDescription: Coastal northwestern mexico to trinidad and suriname, and to far northwestern peru
description: Elusive, chickenlike rail of mangroves, less often occurs in freshwater marshes. Slightly smaller than a Common Gallinule.

name: Slender-tailed Nightjar
rangeDescription: Southeastern south sudan, ethiopia, djibouti, northwestern and southern somalia, uganda, kenya, and northeastern tanzania
description: A slim nightjar with a slightly elongated central tail. Both sexes have a large pale mark in the outer wing and along the sides of the tail, white in males and buff in females.

name: Sumatran Leafbird
rangeDescription: Sumatra
description: Uncommon and declining Sumatran endemic, restricted to foothill forest at 600-1000 meters. A typical leafbird, with a predominantly bright green body in both sexes.

name: James's Flamingo
rangeDescription: High andes of southern peru to northwestern argentina and northern chile
description: Rather local; found at salt lakes and bogs in the high Andes. Associates readily with Chilean and Andean Flamingos, although each species often stays slightly apart within mixed groups.

name: Red-breasted Merganser
rangeDescription: Breeds southern greenland, iceland, northern british isles, and scandinavia to sakhalin and kamchatka peninsulas, and kuril and commander islands (southeastern russia), in south through northern kazakhstan and northeastern china; western alaska mainland through mainland canada from arctic to northern great lakes and eastward to nova scotia; winters to coasts of southern europe, black and caspian seas; japan, korean peninsula, and eastern china; to west-central mexico, gulf coast, and florida
description: Long-bodied duck with a thin bill and shaggy crest. Breeding males have a dark green head, brown breast, and gray sides.

name: Jerdon's Leafbird
rangeDescription: Peninsular india and sri lanka
description: Crisp emerald-green forest-dweller. Male has a dark blue throat patch outlined by a thick black border.

name: Guianan Trogon
rangeDescription: Venezuela, trinidad, the guianas, and adjacent northern brazil
description: Medium-sized, long-tailed, sluggish bird that occurs in a variety of humid forest types. Males are iridescent blue with a yellow belly; females are mostly grayish where males are blue.

name: Fiery-billed Aracari
rangeDescription: Pacific slope of costa rica and western panama (western chiriquí)
description: Aracaris are medium-sized toucans, rather slender and long tailed. Fiery-billed is distinctive: the top half of the bill is bright orange.

name: Luzon Hornbill
rangeDescription: Philippines (luzon, marinduque, and catanduanes)
description: A fairly large bird of lowland and foothill forest on Luzon and neighboring islands. Small for a hornbill.

name: White-spotted Munia
rangeDescription: Lowlands of southern new guinea (lorentz river eastward at least to the kikori river region, and perhaps farther eastward)
description: A small brown bird with a heavy blue bill, rufous underparts, and white spotting across the head, back, and breast. The pale buff rump is conspicuous in flight.

name: Long-billed Crow
rangeDescription: Northern moluccas (morotai, halmahera, kayoa, bacan, obi, and kasiruta)
description: A distinctive crow with a strikingly long bill, noticeable even in flight. Adults have purple-glossed blackish plumage and a prominent pale eye.

name: Chilean Pigeon
rangeDescription: Araucaria and nothofagus forest and adjacent fields of central and southern chile and adjacent argentina
description: Only large native pigeon in its range. Locally fairly common in temperate rainforest, farmland with wooded patches, and matorral with taller trees.

name: Madagascar Sandgrouse
rangeDescription: Arid lowlands of madagascar
description: Brownish bird that is shaped like a large dove. Male has a black front and plain wing with three black bars; female has fine black markings across the back.

name: Bahama Woodstar
rangeDescription: Varied habitats in bahamas (except for inagua group) and the caicos islands
description: A small, long-tailed hummingbird of wooded and scrubby habitats including gardens; most often found feeding on flowers or at hummingbird feeders. Note the male’s iridescent purple throat and forehead and its long, forked tail.
